items.title: [OctoPrint] OctoPrint: Stored XSS via saved connection parameters
items.summary: ImpactOctoPrint versions 2.0.0rc1 up until version 2.0.0rc6 are susceptible to cross-site scripting via a specially crafted default port or baudrate setting on the bundled Serial Connector plugin, supplied via the API as new defaults during a connect request.PatchesThe vulnerability is patched in 2.0.0rc7.WorkaroundCheck config.yaml for Javascript fragments in printerConnection.preferred.parameters.port or printerConnection.preferred.parameters.baudrate. If found, remove them. You can check who of your users had access to your instance since you flashed 2.0.0rc1 or above via auth.log. CreditsThis vulnerability was discovered and responsibly disclosed to OctoPrint by "mahn-don".Timeline2026-10-14: Report received2026-10-14: Report acknowledged2026-10-14: Report verified2026-10-14: Fix ready for 2.0.0rc72026-10-20: CVE requestedReferenceshttps://github.com/OctoPrint/OctoPrint/security/advisories/GHSA-p623-mxf7-qxjmhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-123364https://github.com/OctoPrint/OctoPrint/commit/059495787a1086868a28ba9eca8d089729242646https://github.com/OctoPrint/OctoPrint/releases/tag/2.0.0rc7https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p623-mxf7-qxjm

items.title: [compose-lint] compose-lint: Incomplete fix for GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg: a run stopped at the finding limit quotes a secret from a CI-generated `.env`
items.summary: ImpactThis is an incomplete fix for GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg. 0.32.0 made findings quote the ${NAME} a sibling .env filled in, instead of its value. The same release added a stop at 20,000 findings per document, and that stop is checked before the quoting step. A run that hits it reports the findings graded so far with the resolved values still in them, in text, JSON and SARIF output. That happens with or without --allow-partial-coverage.The attack is the one GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg describes. In a CI workflow that writes secrets into the .env beside the Compose file, a pull request changes a line to image: "${DB_PASSWORD}". It also pushes the document past 20,000 findings, which a few hundred lines can do, because an aliased list is graded once for each service that uses it. The secret's value is quoted in a finding that reaches the job log, the JSON output and the SARIF uploaded to Code Scanning. GitHub masks registered secrets in the job log, but not in uploaded JSON or SARIF artifacts or in Code Scanning alert text. The run exits 2, or 0 with --allow-partial-coverage, after the output has been written.The preconditions are the same as for GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg. The workflow writes secrets into the .env beside the Compose file and runs on pull requests from authors who should not see them, such as a pull_request_target workflow that lints the pull request's files. Pull requests from forks normally run without secrets, so the common setup is not exposed. The inflated document is visible in the pull request, but the workflow runs before anyone reviews it.Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review.Python package. compose-lint 0.32.0. Earlier releases have no finding limit, and their quoting gap is GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg itself.GitHub Action. Action tag v0.32.0 is affected. Tags before v0.22.0 install the newest release unless version: is set, so they currently install 0.32.0.pre-commit hook. rev: v0.32.0.Docker image. composelint/compose-lint:0.32.0, :0.32 and latest are affected when the .env is mounted with the project.PatchesNo fixed release yet.WorkaroundsRun with --no-env, which skips the sibling .env.Don't write secrets into the .env beside the Compose file in a job that lints untrusted pull requests.Reproductionproject/.env          DB_PASSWORD=example-secret      (written by CI, not committed)project/compose.yml   x-p: &p [ ...200 port mappings... ]                      services: one service with image: "${DB_PASSWORD}" and ports: *p,                                plus about 100 more services with ports: *pcompose-lint --format sarif compose.yml exits 2 with "grading stopped at 20000 findings", and the reported findings contain example-secret. The same file with fewer services stays under the limit and quotes ${DB_PASSWORD}. Checked against the 0.32.0 wheel from PyPI, using a synthetic value.Referenceshttps://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/security/advisories/GHSA-rm8w-w798-g545https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-123796https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/pull/978https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/commit/31ec460399e06e98aa0d1cc578368a1960a8a0b3https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/releases/tag/v0.33.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rm8w-w798-g545

items.title: [gpustack] GPUStack: Missing authorization on several cluster and resource endpoints allows cross-user access and cluster takeover
items.summary: ImpactAn authenticated non-administrative user could access a Kubernetes cluster they are not authorized to access through GPUStack's Kubernetes API proxy.The cluster_apiserver_proxy handler did not perform a resource-level authorization check before forwarding requests to the selected cluster. Requests were forwarded through a worker using its Kubernetes ServiceAccount credentials.Depending on the permissions granted to that ServiceAccount, an attacker could read sensitive Kubernetes resources, create or modify workloads, or delete resources and disrupt services. Creating attacker-controlled workloads could result in code execution in the target cluster.Exploitation requires a Kubernetes-provider cluster with a reachable worker. The operations available to the attacker are limited by the worker's ServiceAccount permissions.PatchesFixed in gpustack v2.2.2.WorkaroundsRestrict access to the GPUStack instance to trusted administrator accounts until upgrading.Referenceshttps://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/security/advisories/GHSA-3hch-x692-6qj3https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-103002https://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/pull/5911https://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/pull/5936https://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/commit/363191fa1da7e1426c6041f78b3cf00aff2622fehttps://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/commit/cdd67467e0f314609dc82216e142940d321abfedhttps://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/releases/tag/v2.2.2https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3hch-x692-6qj3

items.title: [gpustack] GPUStack: SAML callback trusts an unverified SAMLResponse, allowing authentication bypass and account takeover
items.summary: ImpactThe callback Base64-decodes the posted XML, reads NameID and attributes, resolves or provisions the user, and mints a gpustack_session JWT — but never calls OneLogin_Saml2_Auth.process_response(), the step that verifies the signature, issuer, audience, destination, and time conditions.No credentials are required, and SAML SSO does not even need to be configured. The callback processes the payload and issues a session regardless of whether SAML is set up, so every deployment is affected, not only SAML-enabled ones. Anyone who can reach the endpoint over the network can authenticate as an arbitrary identity by posting a response that names it:If the name matches an existing user (e.g. an administrator), the attacker receives that user's session — full account takeover, including administrator access.Otherwise, a new non-admin user is provisioned.Administrator access grants full control over the deployment and the infrastructure it manages. Because Response/Assertion IDs are never consumed, a captured signed response also replays indefinitely.Precondition: network reachability to /auth/saml/callback. SAML SSO configuration is not required. A full proof-of-concept is available privately to maintainers.PatchesFixed in gpustack 2.2.2:The SAML callback now validates the response via OneLogin_Saml2_Auth.process_response() — signature, issuer, audience, destination, and time conditions — and rejects responses that fail, so forged or replayed assertions are no longer accepted.The SAML and OIDC login/callback routes are now gated to run only when that provider is the configured active provider, so a deployment that has not enabled the provider no longer parses attacker-supplied IdP payloads.WorkaroundsThere is no effective configuration-level workaround — disabling or not configuring SAML does not mitigate this on affected versions, since the callback runs regardless. Until upgraded, block network access to /auth/saml/callback (e.g. at a reverse proxy / ingress).CreditReported privately by Austin Chu, Sohee Kim, and Corban Villa (UC Berkeleysecurity research project), and independently, earlier, by a researcher who wishes to remain anonymous.Referenceshttps://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/security/advisories/GHSA-62m9-f875-rqw6https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-102894https://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/pull/5753https://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/pull/5923https://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/commit/705edbe1b5feec63959306daecd640e1c70eced2https://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/commit/adc6d82be34e48390720a1361df616e2ea9d6d45https://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/releases/tag/v2.2.2https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-62m9-f875-rqw6

items.title: [ag2] AG2: Newline injection in SandboxShellTool bypasses allowed=[...] and readonly=True, enabling arbitrary command execution
items.summary:
SummarySandboxShellTool's restricted modes — allowed=[...] (explicit command allowlist) and readonly=True (implicit READONLY_COMMANDS allowlist) — can both be bypassed by embedding a newline character inside the command string. The filter only inspects a single-line set of shell metacharacters, but execution runs the raw string through sh -c, where a shell treats an embedded newline exactly like a ; statement separator. An agent (or content that steers the agent, e.g. via prompt injection) can therefore run arbitrary shell commands even when the tool was configured to allow only a specific command prefix or only read-only commands. With the default LocalEnvironment() backend this is a real host subprocess (its own docstring: "Commands run via subprocess on the host, so there is no real isolation"), not an isolated container, so this is full host command execution, not merely an escape from an already-sandboxed environment.DetailsBoth restricted modes are enforced by ShellAdapter._filter() in ag2/tools/sandbox/adapter/shell.py:def _filter(self, command: str) -> str | None:    if self._allowed is not None:        if not any(matches(p, command) for p in self._allowed):            return f"Command not allowed: {command!r}"        if contains_shell_operator(command):            return f"Command not allowed (shell operators are not permitted in restricted mode): {command!r}"    ...readonly=True reuses this exact same branch: SandboxShellTool.__init__ / ShellAdapter.__init__ sets self._allowed = list(READONLY_COMMANDS) when readonly is set and no explicit allowed is given, so both modes share one filter and one bypass.contains_shell_operator() in ag2/tools/sandbox/filter.py checks the command against:_SHELL_OPERATORS: tuple[str, ...] = (">", ">>", "|", ";", "&&", "||", "`", "$(")This tuple has no entry for 
 (or ). matches() only checks that the command starts with an allowed prefix followed by a space or end-of-string; it never inspects the remainder of the string. Execution is:argv = ["sh", "-c", command]...return await sandbox.exec(argv, env=self._env, timeout=self._timeout)A POSIX shell splits sh -c "<line1>
<line2>" into two sequential statements, the same as if they were separated by ;. So a command such as "cat allowed_file.txt
rm -rf /anything":Passes matches("cat", command) — the string starts with "cat ".Passes contains_shell_operator(command) — 
 is not a recognized operator.Reaches sh -c "cat allowed_file.txt
rm -rf /anything", which runs both statements.Proof of ConceptVerified directly against the current main branch (github.com/ag2ai/ag2, commit a05ff1cb6ff4955ef252a4e0d4a27d3a32ad57f0, cloned 2026-09-21), by importing the real ag2/tools/sandbox/filter.py module (stdlib-only, no other AG2 dependencies needed) and reproducing ShellAdapter._filter()'s allowlist branch verbatim:=== allowed=['cat'] ==='cat /etc/passwd; rm -rf /tmp/x'   -> Command not allowed (shell operators are not permitted in restricted mode): ...'cat /etc/passwd && rm -rf /tmp/x' -> Command not allowed (shell operators are not permitted in restricted mode): ...'cat /etc/passwd | rm -rf /tmp/x'  -> Command not allowed (shell operators are not permitted in restricted mode): ...'cat /etc/passwd
rm -rf /tmp/x'   -> None   <-- BYPASS: newline variant is NOT rejected=== readonly=True (uses READONLY_COMMANDS as the allowed list) ==='echo hi
id'                      -> None   <-- BYPASS in readonly mode too=== sh -c really treats the embedded newline as a second statement (mirrors ShellAdapter._exec_async) ===$ sh -c 'echo first-command-output
echo SECOND-STATEMENT-RAN-$((21*2))'first-command-outputSECOND-STATEMENT-RAN-42The three standard chaining attempts (;, &&, |) are correctly rejected by the real filter, confirming it does real work; the newline-separated variant, expressing the same intent, is accepted by the identical filter in both restricted modes, and a real sh -c call confirms the shell executes both statements.ImpactAny agent configured with SandboxShellTool(allowed=[...]) or SandboxShellTool(readonly=True) — the two configurations the tool's own docstring presents as actual security boundaries, as opposed to blocked, which the same docstring explicitly says "is not a security boundary" — can be made to execute arbitrary shell commands via a single embedded newline in the command argument. Because tool arguments are LLM-generated and can be steered by content the agent processes (a fetched document, tool output, or any other text reaching the model — i.e. indirect prompt injection), this is reachable without the operator of the agent writing the malicious command themselves. With the default LocalEnvironment() backend, this is command execution on the host process running the agent, not confined to a container.Suggested RemediationAdd "
" and "" to _SHELL_OPERATORS in ag2/tools/sandbox/filter.py so contains_shell_operator() rejects embedded newlines the same way it rejects ;.More robustly, execute allowlisted/reado

items.title: [compose-lint] compose-lint: A pull request can make compose-lint quote a secret from a CI-generated `.env` into its findings
items.summary: ImpactSince 0.22.0, compose-lint fills in ${VAR} references from the .env beside the Compose file, as Compose does. The documentation says values under environment: are never resolved from a .env, "that is where secrets live". But image: values are resolved, and CL-0004 and CL-0019 quote the resolved image in their message and fix text.Some CI workflows write secrets into that .env before linting or building. In such a workflow, a pull request that changes one line to image: "${DB_PASSWORD}", or image: "nginx:${DB_PASSWORD}", gets the secret's value quoted in a finding. The finding reaches the job log, JSON output, and the SARIF uploaded to Code Scanning. GitHub masks registered secrets in the job log, but not in uploaded JSON or SARIF artifacts or in Code Scanning alert text. The pass/fail result is not affected.This needs a workflow that writes secrets into the .env beside the Compose file and runs on pull requests from authors who should not see them. Pull requests from forks normally run without secrets, so the common setup is not exposed, which is why this is scored as low confidentiality impact. Where the conditions hold, such as a pull_request_target workflow, pull requests from branches in the same repository, or a self-hosted runner that keeps a populated .env in the checkout, the whole value is disclosed.Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review.GitHub Action. Action tags v0.22.0 through v0.31.0 install their own compose-lint version and are affected. Earlier tags install the newest release unless version: is set, and so currently install an affected one.Docker image. composelint/compose-lint tags 0.22.0 through 0.31.0, the matching minor tags, and latest are affected when the .env is mounted with the project.PatchesFixed in 0.32.0. Rules still grade the value the sibling .env substituted, but findings, fix guidance and notes quote the ${NAME} reference in its place, in text, JSON and SARIF. A value shorter than 8 characters is shown as written, because short values are also words the guidance itself uses; docs/what-a-run-reads.md states this limit.WorkaroundsUpgrade to 0.32.0 or later.Run with --no-env, which skips the sibling .env.Don't write secrets into the .env beside the Compose file in a job that lints untrusted pull requests.Reproductionproject/.env          DB_PASSWORD=example-secret      (written by CI, not committed)project/compose.yml   services: {web: {image: "${DB_PASSWORD}"}}compose-lint --format sarif compose.yml reports CL-0004 with the message Image 'example-secret' has no tag, ....Referenceshttps://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/security/advisories/GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrghttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-123372https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/pull/944https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/commit/977da9724789264c2662afe47f79220e915442c2https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/releases/tag/v0.32.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg

items.title: [compose-lint] compose-lint: `fix --apply` can delete a line the user did not select, including a security setting
items.summary: Impactcompose-lint fix --apply converts the line numbers its fixers work with into positions in the file. The YAML parser treats a lone carriage return, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029 as line breaks, but the conversion counted only \n. One of those characters inside a quoted value, which most editors and diff views don't show, shifted every later edit down by one line.A Compose file from a pull request can use this to make a fix delete the line after the one it meant to change. For example, fixing CL-0014 (logging: driver: none) instead removes driver: none and the following networks: [internal], moving the service off an internal-only network onto the default bridge. The result is still valid Compose, every check fix runs after editing passes, and the command reports applied 1 fix(es) and exits 0. A later compose-lint check passes too, because no rule requires networks:. The dry-run diff (without --apply) does show the removed lines, but --apply prints only the note for the fix that was selected.A related crash on the same files could empty the SARIF output for every file in the run. GitHub Code Scanning rejects an empty SARIF upload, which fails the step, so that part does not report a false clean result there.Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review.Docker image. composelint/compose-lint tags 0.9.0 through 0.17.0, and the matching minor tags, are affected when used to run fix --apply. Fixed from 0.18.0.The GitHub Action does not run fix and is not affected.PatchesFixed in 0.18.0. Line splitting and position conversion now share one definition of a line break, so they can't disagree. A Compose file containing an ambiguous line break (a lone \r, U+0085, U+2028 or U+2029) is refused with exit code 2, because no line numbering is correct for both the parser and the editor. CRLF and LF files are unaffected.WorkaroundsUpgrade to 0.18.0 or later.On older versions, review the dry-run diff before --apply, and don't run fix --apply over files from untrusted pull requests.Reproductionservices:  web:    image: nginx@sha256:<digest>    labels:      note: "line one<U+2028>line two"    logging:      driver: none    networks: [internal]networks:  internal:    internal: truecompose-lint fix --apply compose.yml on 0.17.0 reports applied 1 fix(es), exits 0, and removes both driver: none and networks: [internal].Referenceshttps://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/security/advisories/GHSA-65v8-q222-64xxhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-123370https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/pull/547https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/pull/549https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/commit/c9d453a6a69c076788fe1db05cb54684a616d1dehttps://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/commit/cbbf886d91347dea9c51b584eb50088e70007d0dhttps://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/releases/tag/v0.18.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-65v8-q222-64xx

items.title: [compose-lint] compose-lint: .env read through a symlink outside the project can expose the CI job's environment
items.summary: Impactcompose-lint fills in ${VAR} references from the .env file next to the Compose file. It is meant to read nothing outside the project directory, and env_file:, include: and extends: paths are checked for that. The .env read is not. If .env is a symlink, compose-lint follows it wherever it points.A pull request can add a .env symlink to any file on the CI runner and a Compose file that references a variable from it. compose-lint substitutes the value and quotes it in finding messages, which go to the log and to JSON and SARIF output.The worst target is /proc/self/environ, the linter's own environment. The Compose file only needs to reference the name of the first variable in it: because that file separates variables with NUL bytes rather than newlines, the substituted value is the entire rest of the environment. On a CI runner that environment holds whatever the workflow put there, including secrets. GitHub masks registered secrets in the job log, but not in uploaded JSON or SARIF artifacts or in Code Scanning alert text.An include: entry's project_directory: has the same gap from 0.28.0: a directory symlink named there makes compose-lint read .env from wherever the link points.Pull requests from forks normally run without secrets, and GitHub masks registered secrets in the job log, so in the common setup what can be read is runner metadata and whatever unmasked values the job's environment holds. That is why this is scored as low confidentiality impact. The impact is high in a job that runs untrusted pull requests with secrets in its environment, such as a pull_request_target workflow, or on a CI system that does not mask secrets, and also wherever the JSON or SARIF output is uploaded. The pass/fail result is not affected.Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review.PatchesFixed in 0.31.0. Every .env read now applies the same containment check as env_file:. A .env that resolves outside the project is treated as missing and reported as an unread input. A project_directory: that resolves outside the project is refused, and that entry's files resolve against their own directories. A .env line containing a NUL byte is skipped.WorkaroundsRun with --no-env, which skips the sibling .env entirely.Don't run compose-lint on untrusted pull requests in a job whose environment holds secrets.Reproductionproject/.env -> /proc/self/environ      (symlink)project/compose.yml:  services:    web:      image: "${FIRST_VAR_NAME}"compose-lint check compose.yml --format json quotes the environment in the CL-0004 message ("Image '...' has no tag").Referenceshttps://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/security/advisories/GHSA-6wcv-rj3c-mhv3https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-123368https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/pull/917https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/commit/c43204ad4dab11d54e20574a52bc4e5835246ca5https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/releases/tag/v0.31.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6wcv-rj3c-mhv3

items.title: [compose-lint] compose-lint: A committed symlink makes compose-lint quote a file from outside the project into its output
items.summary: ImpactLike Docker Compose, compose-lint follows symlinks when it reads a project's files. Unlike Compose, compose-lint up to 0.24.0 could then put the contents of a file from outside the project into its output, where the author of a pull request can read it.A pull request can commit a symlink, under a name compose-lint reads, pointing at a file on the CI runner:The Compose file itself (0.2.0–0.24.0). A compose.yml that is a symlink, whether the pre-commit hook passes its name or the Action or a bare run finds it.compose.override.yml (0.22.0–0.24.0), which compose-lint merges automatically.A COMPOSE_FILE entry (0.22.0–0.24.0) in a .env beside the Compose file.When the target is not valid YAML, the parse error quotes the line it failed on. Docker Compose, given the same file, reports only a line number. That line reaches standard error (the job log), JSON errors[], and the SARIF toolExecutionNotifications, which the Action uploads to Code Scanning.A fourth route: from 0.23.0, a symlinked env_file: target makes CL-0020 and CL-0021 report the credential-like key names in a file outside the project. Values are not printed.What can be read is one line of a file chosen by path, at the point where the YAML parser fails, which the attacker cannot choose; or key names. A symlink to /proc/self/environ gave neither in testing. The pass/fail result is not affected. On a public repository the job log is visible to the pull request's author.Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review.GitHub Action. Action tags v0.18.0 through v0.24.0 install their own compose-lint version and are affected. Earlier tags install the newest release unless version: is set; they were affected while that was 0.24.0 or earlier.Docker image. composelint/compose-lint tags 0.3.3 through 0.24.0, and the matching minor tags, are affected. Inside the container a symlink resolves within the container, so what can be read is the container's own files and anything mounted into it. Fixed from 0.25.0.PatchesFixed in 0.25.0. Parse errors no longer quote the source line; the error and its line and column are kept. env_file: targets and COMPOSE_FILE entries that resolve outside the project are also refused, with the existing outside-the-project note. Symlinks that stay inside the project still work.From 0.25.0 through 0.31.0, a committed symlink to a target that is itself a Compose file could still be read, and its values could reach findings. 0.32.0 stops following a discovered, named or override Compose file whose link leaves the checkout.A related gap for the sibling .env file is covered by GHSA-6wcv-rj3c-mhv3, and one for a symlinked .compose-lint.yml by GHSA-88f4-frh5-gmcr.WorkaroundsUpgrade to 0.25.0 or later.On older versions, don't run compose-lint on untrusted pull requests on a machine whose files outside the checkout hold credentials. --no-env closes the COMPOSE_FILE and env_file: routes, but not the others.Reproductionproject/compose.yml -> /path/outside/project/credentials   (symlink)compose-lint --format sarif compose.yml on 0.24.0 exits 2, and the SARIF notification quotes a line of the linked file. On 0.25.0 the error gives only the line and column.Referenceshttps://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/security/advisories/GHSA-whr6-fgpq-fpv9https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-123373https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/pull/721https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/commit/364814329417dbbc34d1ad2f3981f8a7a023799ehttps://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/releases/tag/v0.25.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-whr6-fgpq-fpv9

items.title: [compose-lint] compose-lint: Compose file text can issue GitHub Actions workflow commands through the compose-lint Action
items.summary: ImpactThe GitHub Actions runner treats certain text in a step's output as commands. The legacy form, ##[command], is recognized anywhere in a line. compose-lint's text report prints service names, environment keys and lines of the Compose file, and it does not neutralize ##[. Inside the compose-lint Action, a Compose file from a pull request can therefore:create fake error or warning annotations on the pull request (##[error], ##[warning])fold the rest of the log, including the real verdict, out of sight (##[group])blank out chosen strings for the rest of the log (##[add-mask])GitHub has postponed removing the deprecated set-output log command, so the runner still honors it. A test run of the Action on a GitHub-hosted runner confirmed that a ::set-output line from a Compose file is processed. Whether it can override the Action's own sarif-written output, which decides whether the SARIF upload step runs, has not been tested.The exit code and the pass/fail result are not affected. Azure Pipelines parses the same ##[ syntax, so the pip package is listed for anyone printing the text report in other CI systems.Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review.PatchesFixed in 0.31.0. The Action stops the runner from processing workflow commands while compose-lint's output is printed, using a random stop-commands token. The text report also escapes ##[, and :: at the start of a line, in anything taken from the Compose file.WorkaroundsIn your own workflow, wrap the compose-lint step in ::stop-commands::<random token> and ::<random token>::.Use --format json or --format sarif rather than the text report when linting untrusted pull requests.Reproductionservices:  web:    image: "nginx:1.25"    environment:      "##[error]DB_PASSWORD": placeholder  "##[group]svc":    image: "nginx:1.25"    privileged: trueRun through the Action, this produces a fake error annotation and folds the remaining log lines, including the FAIL verdict, into a collapsed group.Referenceshttps://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/security/advisories/GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-123369https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/pull/918https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/commit/672bd11145621f787c295fb11f3a859cdec1b38dhttps://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/releases/tag/v0.31.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6

items.title: [compose-lint] compose-lint: A `.compose-lint.yml` symlinked outside the project is read, and a parse error quotes part of the target
items.summary: Impactcompose-lint automatically reads a .compose-lint.yml policy file beside the Compose file. It is meant to read nothing outside the project directory, but it follows that file if it is a symlink, wherever it points.A pull request can commit .compose-lint.yml as a symlink to a file on the CI runner. If the target is not valid YAML, the error compose-lint reports quotes part of the line the parser failed on. That quote reaches the job log (standard error), JSON errors[], and the SARIF toolExecutionNotifications, which the Action uploads to Code Scanning. The run exits 2.What can be read is small. The quote is cut to about 30 characters around the error position, and the attacker cannot choose which line of the target the parser fails on. For an INI-style credentials file, this was the start of the second line (aws_access_key_id =  followed by the first characters of the value). Targets in KEY=value form, and YAML files that parse, disclosed no values in testing. The pass/fail result is not affected. On a public repository, the job log is visible to the pull request's author.The Compose file loader stopped quoting source lines in parse errors in 0.25.0 (GHSA-whr6-fgpq-fpv9). The policy loader did not.Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review.GitHub Action. Action tags v0.18.0 through v0.31.0 install their own compose-lint version and are affected. Earlier tags install the newest release unless version: is set, and so currently install an affected one.Docker image. composelint/compose-lint tags 0.3.3 through 0.31.0, the matching minor tags, and latest are affected. Inside the container, a symlink resolves within the container, so what can be read is the container's own files and anything mounted into it.PatchesFixed in 0.32.0. A .compose-lint.yml discovered in the working directory that resolves outside it is refused with exit 2 rather than read, and a policy parse error no longer quotes the line it failed on, matching the Compose loader. --config is read as given. 0.32.0 also stops following a Compose file that is a symlink to a target outside the checkout.WorkaroundsUpgrade to 0.32.0 or later.Run with an explicit --config pointing at a policy file inside the project; the automatic lookup is then skipped.Don't run compose-lint on untrusted pull requests on a machine whose files outside the checkout hold credentials.Reproductionproject/.compose-lint.yml -> /path/outside/project/credentials   (symlink)project/compose.yml          services: {web: {image: nginx:1.27}}compose-lint --format sarif compose.yml exits 2, and the notification text quotes the start of the target's second line.Referenceshttps://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/security/advisories/GHSA-88f4-frh5-gmcrhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-123371https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/pull/943https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/commit/e80547d33b2114040c4bc0e34ef210aee51f5058https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/releases/tag/v0.32.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-88f4-frh5-gmcr
